hook.line: There's a new marketing trend that looks like real-life Photoshop
hook.visual: Presenter cut out at the bottom over a clip of a man whose flat cardboard turns into giant hands holding a wrap and a red cup by 1.12 s; yellow-highlighted word captions at top

beats.what: Trend named over the reveal clip: cardboard flips into giant hands holding a wrap and a drink
Fast cut run (shots under 1 s) showing how the cardboard hands are made in a print shop
Stores leave the hands out; close-ups of cutting and assembling
Back to the hero clip: 'share on social media'
Second example: a giant hand holding a phone and a microphone
Real store example: staff behind giant ice-cream hands, screen splits into two clips
Payoff number: costs less than $100 to make
Follow CTA over a last making-of clip, then an end card

characters.enters: Flipped up from a flat sheet in the first second
characters.acts: Hold oversized products in front of people's faces, then appear being printed and cut
characters.exits: Hard cut to the next clip

why_it_works: Result first: the finished illusion is on screen in the first second, before any explanation, so viewers stay to learn how it's made
34 cuts per minute with a median shot of 0.87 s keeps the eye busy while the speaker stays on screen in the corner the whole time
A concrete, low number (under $100) turns a curiosity into something the viewer could copy
Word-by-word captions with one yellow word give a reading rhythm even with sound off
weaknesses: The presenter cutout is small and mostly decorative; he adds little beyond the voice
86% of the text sits outside the safe area at the very top edge
The CTA is a generic 'follow me' tacked onto the end
for_robert: Copy the prop reveal: open on Fred's prop already doing the trick in the first second (the result), then explain; keep his face in a fixed corner while the product clips change under it.
